shortcut-section.title: Hold a shortcut and move the mouse

animation-time.tooltip: How long the cube takes to rotate to the new workspace.

last-first-gap.description: Leave a gap between the last and first workspace
last-first-gap.tooltip:
When enabled, the workspaces cover only half a circle, so switching from the last to the first workspace rotates back through all of them. When disabled, the workspaces form a closed cube and wrapping around takes the shortest way.

This option is linked to Cinnamon's "Allow cycling through workspaces" setting (System Settings > Workspaces): turning cycling on turns this gap off, and turning cycling off turns the gap on. You can still change this option here, but the next change to the Cinnamon setting will override it, and so will disabling and re-enabling this extension.

window-parallax.tooltip: How far windows float in front of the cube faces while it rotates. 0 keeps them flat on the faces.

auto-zoom-out.description: Zoom out while the cube moves (%)
auto-zoom-out.tooltip: While the cube rotates, it moves back until it looks this much smaller than the screen, then comes forward again as it stops. When you rotate the cube with the mouse, it zooms out as you start moving the mouse. 0 turns it off.

panel-mode.description: Panels while the cube is shown
panel-mode.tooltip: On the cube faces: every face shows the panels of its monitor, which turn with the cube. Above the cube: the panels stay where they are and the cube turns behind them. Hidden: the cube is drawn above the panels. The panels themselves are not changed.

per-monitor-perspective.description: Correct the perspective on each monitor
per-monitor-perspective.tooltip: With several monitors, Cinnamon looks at the whole desktop from a single point in front of its center, so a cube on a monitor away from the center is seen from the side and looks skewed. This shows each monitor's cube as seen from straight in front of that monitor.

enable-edge-switch.description: Switch workspaces by pushing a dragged window against the screen edge
enable-edge-switch.tooltip: While dragging a window, push it against the left or right edge of the screen to rotate to the next workspace. The window comes along.

edge-switch-pressure.tooltip: How far you have to push the mouse into the screen edge, within one second, before the workspace switches. Higher values make it less likely to switch by accident, for example when you only want to tile the window.

enable-edge-push.description: Switch workspaces by pushing the mouse against the screen edge
enable-edge-push.tooltip: Push the mouse pointer against the left or right edge of the screen to rotate to the next workspace. Edges between two monitors don't count.

edge-push-action.tooltip: Free rotation lets you turn the cube with the mouse, like the free rotation hot corner action. Left click or Enter switches to the workspace in front, right click or Esc goes back.

edge-push-pressure.tooltip: How hard you have to push the mouse into the screen edge before the workspace switches. Higher values make accidental switches less likely.

edge-push-modifier.tooltip: Only switch when this key is held while pushing against the edge.

edge-peek.tooltip: How far the cube turns towards the next workspace while you push, before it commits. 0 switches without a preview.

enable-panorama.description: Show a panorama around the cube
enable-panorama.tooltip: Instead of black, show a 360° panorama image behind the cube. It turns with the cube and tilts with it.

background-panorama.tooltip: A 360° panorama in equirectangular projection (twice as wide as it is high), as used for photo spheres. Sites such as Poly Haven offer free ones.

cube-shortcut.tooltip: Keep the shortcut's modifier keys held and move the mouse anywhere on the screen: sideways rotates the cube, up and down tilts it, the scroll wheel zooms. Release the keys (or click) to switch to the workspace in front, or press Esc to go back.

enable-panel-dragging.description: Rotate the cube by dragging an empty part of a panel
enable-panel-dragging.tooltip: Hold the left mouse button on a panel, away from any applet, and move the mouse. Moving sideways rotates the cube, moving up or down tilts it, and the scroll wheel zooms in and out. Release the button to switch to the workspace in front, or press Esc to go back.

mouse-rotation-speed.tooltip: How far the cube rotates for a given mouse movement.

do-explode.description: Spread the windows apart when the cube is tilted

panorama-info.tooltip: Use a 360° panorama in equirectangular projection: twice as wide as it is high, as used for photo spheres. JPEG and PNG always work; HDR formats such as .exr and .hdr only if your system can read them. A width of 4K to 8K looks good. The first time a new panorama is used, it is converted into a cube map in the background, which can take a few seconds. The result is cached in ~/.cache/desktop-cube-reloaded, so later it loads right away.

rotating-info.tooltip: Move sideways: rotate the cube Move up or down: tilt the cube Scroll wheel: zoom in and out Esc: go back to the workspace you started on When you release the shortcut's keys (or the mouse button, when dragging a panel), the cube switches to the workspace facing you. If the mouse is still moving, the cube keeps turning a little in that direction.

hot-corner-top-left.tooltip: Pick a cube action to trigger it by pushing the mouse into this corner of the screen. If Cinnamon already uses the corner for something else, that action is kept as the first item of this list: pick it again to put the corner back the way it was. The hover delay and whether corners work over fullscreen windows are set in System Settings → Hot Corners.

If Cinnamon already uses the corner for something else, that action is kept as the first item of this list: pick it again to put the corner back the way it was. The hover delay and whether corners work over fullscreen windows are set in System Settings → Hot Corners.

The hover delay and whether corners work over fullscreen windows are set in System Settings → Hot Corners.

hot-corner-info.description: 💡 What the cube actions do (see tooltip)
hot-corner-info.tooltip: Rotate with the mouse: move the mouse to turn the cube, no button or key held. Left-click (or Enter) switches to the workspace facing you; right-click (or Esc) goes back. Rotate left / right: switch to the workspace on the left / right, like Ctrl+Alt+Left/Right. Left-click in the corner to keep going. These are the same corners as in System Settings → Hot Corners, where they show up as commands named cube-free-rotate, cube-rotate-left and cube-rotate-right. If this extension is turned off, those corners do nothing.

open-workspace-settings.tooltip: Opens System Settings → Workspaces, where you can turn on "Allow cycling through workspaces" (linked to the gap option above) and change the workspace OSD.

open-hot-corner-settings.tooltip: Opens System Settings → Hot Corners, where you can set the hover delay of each corner and whether it works over fullscreen windows.
